results.channel_c_verbatim: Platforms such as The Collective Intelligence Project’s WeVal now host mental health blueprints (suicidality, psychosis, and cultural nuance), but these too largely rate the appropriateness of final responses, not the path that led there
results.sources_checked: Finding: Weval (Collective Intelligence Project) aggregate model card for Claude 3.5 Sonnet, https://weval.org/cards/claude-3-5-sonnet, dated 2025-08-12; card re-fetched and the finding quote verified character-for-character 2026-08-29 ('The model exhibits inconsistent safety performance in high-stakes mental health scenarios, particularly when not given a strong system prompt. It can provide direct answers to dangerous queries or collude with delusions'), with 'Mental Health Safety & Global Nuance (19th percentile, underperformed peers)' confirmed on the card. Company identified as Anthropic from models_systems. CHANNEL A BATTERY (all searches run 2026-08-29). [1] Company newsroom/blog: full sitemap crawl of anthropic.com (https://www.anthropic.com/sitemap.xml, 522 URLs, all fetched and grepped) and of claude.com (230 English-language /blog/ and /news pages). Not found: zero occurrences of 'Weval'/'weval' on any anthropic.com or claude.com page. Three anthropic.com pages mention 'Collective Intelligence Project', none referencing this finding: (a) 'Collective Constitutional AI: Aligning a Language Model with Public Input', 2023-10-17 - INVALIDATED under s8 negative-lag rule (pre-dates the finding by ~22 months; a standing 2023 research collaboration, not a response); (b) 'Anthropic opens Bengaluru office and announces new partnerships across India', 2026-02-16 - post-dates the finding but concerns building India-local evaluations with Karya and CIP 'across domains like agriculture and law', no reference to Weval model cards or mental-health safety, so not causally attributable; (c) 'An update on our election safeguards', 2026-04-24 - post-dates the finding but concerns a CIP review of 'model behaviors around freedom of expression, including political conversations', a different domain, not causally attributable. [2] Model/system cards: fetched and text-searched Claude Sonnet 4.5 (2025-09-29), Claude Haiku 4.5 (2025-10-15), Claude Opus 4.5 (2025-11-24), Claude Sonnet 4.6 (2026-02-17), Claude Opus 4.6 (2026-02), Claude Mythos Preview + Alignment Risk Update (2026-04-07), Claude Fable 5 & Claude Mythos 5 (2026-06-09), Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Opus 5, plus the Anthropic Transparency Hub system-card summaries. Not found: zero occurrences of 'Weval' or 'Collective Intelligence' in any post-finding Anthropic system card. [3] Safety/deployment hubs, advisories and changelogs: anthropic.com/transparency (119k chars, 0 hits), Responsible Scaling Policy v3.0 (2026-02-24, 0 hits), anthropic.com/coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure, docs.claude.com release notes (overview, api, claude-apps), status.claude.com/history. Not found: no mention of Weval, CIP or these model cards. [4] Company response inside the evaluator's own report: weval.org card fetched 2026-08-29 - the word 'Anthropic' occurs 0 times; the card carries no quoted company statement. [5] Open-web location pass for company primary sources: Bing HTML queries ('anthropic weval "collective intelligence project"', 'site:anthropic.com weval', 'anthropic "weval" claude response'), Marginalia ('anthropic weval'), Google News RSS ('"Weval" Anthropic' - 0 items). Not found: no Anthropic primary document responding to the Weval cards. WebSearch tool budget for this session was exhausted (200/200) before use; Bing/Marginalia/Google-News RSS via the fetch helper were used instead, and news articles are in any case never Channel A evidence. ON-TOPIC BUT NON-ATTRIBUTABLE (checked and rejected): 'Building safeguards for Claude' (2025-08-12) documents the pre-existing ThroughLine crisis-support partnership and self-harm/mental-health training work with no reference to Weval - pre-existing/standing work under s8; 'Protecting the wellbeing of our users' (2025-12-18) reports suicide/self-harm evaluations run without a system prompt (Opus 4.1 97.2% on clear-risk single-turn), the ThroughLine crisis banner and the IASP collaboration, but names no external evaluator and does not reference Weval or CIP, so it is not causally attributable to this finding. Additional negative-lag invalidation for this row: the Claude 3.5 Sonnet model card/addendum (June 2024) and 'Building safeguards for Claude' (2025-08-12, same-day, lag 0) cannot count - the former pre-dates the finding, and the latter is not a documented coordinated disclosure (it contains no reference to Weval or CIP). CHANNEL B BATTERY (all searches run 2026-08-29). UK: Hansard search API (Commons+Lords, Members, Contributions, Written Statements, Written Answers, Debates, Committees, Divisions) - 'Weval': Not found, 0 records of every type; '"Collective Intelligence Project"': 1 contribution returned (Dame Chi Onwurah, on digital infrastructure/Post Office software), a loose-token false positive unrelated to AI evaluation. gov.uk search API - 'Weval': Not found, total 0; '"Collective Intelligence Project"': 4 results, all 2023 (Frontier AI Taskforce first/second progress reports, Taskforce personnel announcement, AI Safety Summit introduction), all pre-dating the finding and unrelated - INVALIDATED under s8. NCSC site search 'weval': Not found, empty result page. ICO site search: endpoint returned 404 (blocked). US: Federal Register full-text API - 'Weval' count 0; '"Collective Intelligence Project"' count 0. NIST site search 'weval': Not found, empty results. FTC site search 'weval': Not found, empty results. Congress.gov search returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare challenge) and both api.congress.gov and api.govinfo.gov returned HTTP 429 OVER_RATE_LIMIT on the shared DEMO_KEY across three attempts - the congressional full-text index could NOT be searched this session and is recorded as blocked, not as a verified absence. EU/other: European Commission search ('weval') returned 'No results found'. No jurisdiction produced any official government document citing Weval, the Collective Intelligence Project card, or this finding. CHANNEL C LOG (2026-08-29). Academic: OpenAlex full-text search 'weval.org' returns exactly 1 work - Nunes A et al., 'It Is the Journey, Not the Destination: Moving From End Points to Trajectories When Assessing Chatbot Mental Health Safety', JMIR Mental Health, doi 10.2196/91454, PMC13052998 (OpenAlex date 2026-03-04; Europe PMC first publication date 2026-04-06), which cites Weval's mental-health blueprints at refs 22-23 (weval.org/analysis/mh_z_tests__mh1, accessed 2025-11-29; the 'Stanford HAI Mental Health Safety: LLM Appropriateness in Crisis Scenarios' run, accessed 2026-03-16) - the same blueprint underlying this finding. Also arXiv:2511.05613v2 'Who Evaluates AI's Social Impacts? Mapping Coverage and Gaps in First and Third Party Evaluations' (2025-11-06), which states it incorporated 'leaderboards from Weval'; and arXiv:2602.20042v2 'AI Alignment Breaks at the Edge' (2026-02-23), which describes the Weval platform and cites CIP. Semantic Scholar API returned HTTP 429 on all attempts (rate-limited, no key). Press: Google News RSS ('Weval AI evaluation', '"Weval" Anthropic', '"Collective Intelligence Project" Weval') surfaced Tech Policy Press, 'Women, Peace and Security Frameworks Must Apply to Defense AI' (2026-04-21), which reports benchmark results run on Weval.org, plus a CIP fellowship call (2026-04-16) and passing mentions in Communications of the ACM (2026-02-24, page 403) and ICTworks (2026-01-20, page 404). Not found: no independent press coverage of this Claude model card or of the mental-health finding itself. Social: Hacker News Algolia API - 'weval' matches an unrelated WebAssembly compiler project; the six comments containing 'weval.org' are posted by the Weval maintainer (evaluator's own promotion, circular and excluded). Not found: no notable independent public discussion of this model card.
results.notes: Action Level None: the five-source Channel A battery was exhausted with a complete crawl of both Anthropic web properties (752 pages) and every Anthropic system card published between the finding and 2026-08; Anthropic has never referenced Weval. Anthropic's substantial post-finding mental-health work (crisis classifier and ThroughLine banner, IASP collaboration, no-system-prompt suicide/self-harm evaluations reported 2025-12-18) is on the same topic but is standing/independent work with no attribution to this evaluator, so under s8 it is not a response. Channel B caveat: the US congressional full-text index (congress.gov search 403; api.congress.gov and api.govinfo.gov 429) could not be reached; Federal Register, NIST, FTC, Hansard, gov.uk, NCSC and EC were all searched and returned nothing.
